title: The board pack refresh failed at 06:17
seo: Power BI incident response scenario: the production semantic model refresh failed before the CFO's board meeting. Triage, mitigate, find the root causes, communicate and write the postmortem.
summary: The Finance Board Pack model failed to refresh at 06:17. The CFO presents from it at 08:30. Decide what to do in the next hour, then fix it properly.

verified.context: Refresh troubleshooting and gateway data source docs (Microsoft Learn, Sept 2026)

story: Finance closed May on Friday 5 June at 18:00. The Finance Board Pack model refreshes every day at 05:30 and normally finishes by 06:10. Sam, the model's listed owner, is on holiday this week.
impact: The CFO presents May results to the board at 08:30. If she presents wrong numbers, or cancels because she can't trust them, that's a board-level incident. The clock matters as much as the cause.

messages.subject: Refresh failed: Finance Board Pack
body: Your semantic model Finance Board Pack in workspace Finance Board Pack couldn't be refreshed. DM_GWPipeline_Gateway_MashupDataAccessError. (Delivered to sam.patel@northwind.example; out-of-office reply sent.)
Morning! The board pack dashboard says "Data refreshed: Sun 7 Jun 06:05". Sarah presents at 08:30 from it. Is that OK? Should it say today? I'm panicking a bit.

messages.subject: Board pack
body: I'm told there's a problem with the board pack data. I need to know by 07:45 whether I can present from it, and if not, what I should use instead. Sarah
Heard there's a refresh issue. Nothing failed on our side overnight; the DW loads were all green. Shout if you need anything.

evidence.title: refresh_error.json
evidence.desc: Error details from the refresh history in the Service.

evidence.title: vw_customer_columns.csv
evidence.desc: Columns of dbo.vw_Customer yesterday and today (from the DW's schema history).

evidence.title: change_calendar.csv
evidence.desc: IT change calendar for the weekend.

evidence.title: Finance close calendar (May 2026)
body:
- Last postings for May: Fri 5 Jun, 18:00. Ledger locked for May after that.
- Board pack figures = May closed ledger. June postings are not shown in the pack.

tasks: By 07:45: decide whether Sarah can present from the dashboard as it is, and tell her. Base it on evidence, not hope.
Restore a successful refresh as soon as it is safe, without making an emergency change that could make things worse.
Find every root cause (there may be more than one) and fix them permanently.
Keep stakeholders updated on a schedule, even when there's no news.
Write the incident report and the postmortem with preventive actions and owners.

deliverables.t: The 07:45 answer to the CFO, with the evidence behind it
Incident report: summary, impact, detection, timeline, root cause, mitigation, permanent fix
Blameless postmortem with preventive actions, owners and dates

hints: Before fixing anything, answer the CFO's real question: does Sunday 06:05's data contain everything the board pack shows? Compare the refresh history with the close calendar.
refresh_error.json lists two separate errors on two separate sources. Find a weekend change in change_calendar.csv that explains each one.

One fix belongs in the model (or the view), the other in the gateway connection. A full refresh takes ~35 minutes: work out the latest time you can start one and still be safe, and whether you need it at all before 08:30.

rubric.good: Establishes by 07:45 that Sunday's data already contains the closed May ledger, so the CFO can present; says so clearly with the data timestamp.
Both causes identified with evidence: CHG-4471 renamed CustomerSegment, CHG-4472 rotated the treasury service account password.
Safe mitigation (credential update, Power Query or view alias), a verified refresh, and permanent changes: contract for the view, credential managed by owner, alerts to a team.
Scheduled updates; the CFO gets a yes/no with reasons; the postmortem is blameless and readable by non-engineers.
Actions with owners and dates: alert routing, schema change notification/contract, credential rotation process, failure-tolerant design.

retro: What would you have done at 07:05 if the close had been on Sunday night instead of Friday?
Which of the two causes was a process failure and which was a technical one?
The failure email went to someone on holiday. What should alerting look like for a SEV1 model?
How would you know about the next upstream schema change before it breaks you?
